shape_hint: A swing (hinge) bolt: a threaded rod (thread length b, diameter d1) whose head end is a flat forged eye / lug of round outline with outside diameter d3 and thickness s; a transverse pin hole of diameter d2 passes through the eye so the bolt can pivot on a pin. A small radius blends the rod into the eye. Type A has a thicker, slightly smaller-diameter eye than B/C.

role_map.d3_min_A: eye outside diameter min, type A
role_map.d3_min_BC: eye outside diameter min, types B and C

notes: DIN 444 (04/1983) eye bolts 'Augenschrauben' = swing bolts: hinged on a pin, NOT for lifting. Forms: A (forged, larger eye), B and C (machined; same eye dimensions, differ in thread/shank design). b is the thread length for nominal length l <= 125; b for 125 < l <= 200 is: M8 28, M10 32, M12 36, M16 44, M20 52, M24 60; b for l > 200 is: M12 49, M16 57, M20 65, M24 73 (all mm; '-' = not used). Row M5 and M6 exist only up to l<=125. Bracketed non-preferred sizes (M27, M33, M39) and M30/M36 dropped (see dropped). Radius r (2.5, 4, 4, 4, 6, 6, 6, 10 for M5..M24) is listed by only two sources, so it is not published. Slot/tolerance classes (d2 H9, d2 min=nominal, max = nominal + 0.03..0.05) not tabulated.

fasten.it uses different symbols: its 'd1' column is the pin hole (DIN d2) and its 'd2 min/max' is the eye OD (DIN d3); Fuller labels the eye OD 'Sd' (torqbolt 'd b'). Mapping for those two sources is by numeric identity, header-proven only in fasteners.eu (and Boltport for d2/d3 max).
no source defines d3 (eye OD) / s (eye thickness) in words; roles rest on DIN 444 symbol convention + geometry (flag only).
fasteners.eu b rows are unlabeled/shifted (stray '0' cell, M27 '6' typo) - b for l<=125 read positionally; fasten.it, Fuller, Boltport label it 'b (l<=125)'.
producer note 'fasteners.eu and Fuller have the same structure' is just the DIN table structure; no shared typos found (fasteners.eu typos not in Fuller).
